outline.description: Introduce the problem of finetuning very large language models (LLMs), the computational and memory challenges, and the goals of QLoRA. Present a high-level overview of the method and the key contributions of the paper (NF4, Double Quantization, Paged Optimizers, and LoRA-on-quantized-weights). Motivate why this topic matters for students, researchers, and practitioners.
sections: Why finetune LLMs? Benefits and use cases
The scaling and resource problem: memory and cost at large model scales
Existing strategies: full finetuning, PEFT, quantization for inference
High-level idea of QLoRA and the Guanaco models
Summary of paper contributions and learning objectives for the textbook

outline.description: Provide necessary background on LLM architectures, training vs. finetuning, sources of memory usage during training, and a primer on common finetuning techniques. This chapter ensures readers have the baseline knowledge needed for later chapters.
sections: Decoder-only, encoder-only, and encoder-decoder architectures
Pretraining versus finetuning: objectives and differences
Memory costs in training: parameters, activations, optimizer states, gradients
Gradient checkpointing and mixed precision training
Parameter-Efficient Finetuning (PEFT) strategies: an overview

outline.description: Explain quantization principles, error sources, block-wise quantization, and practical issues like outliers. Formalize quantization and dequantization with math and examples to build intuition for NF4 and Double Quantization.
sections: What is quantization? Goals and basic definitions
Uniform versus non-uniform quantization
Block-wise quantization and the role of quantization constants
Dequantization and numerical error analysis
Outliers, dynamic ranges, and why blockwise quantization helps
Examples: int8, float8 and conventional 4-bit quantization approaches

outline.chapter_title: 4. Low-Rank Adapters (LoRA) and PEFT in Depth
outline.description: Dive deep into Low-Rank Adapters: mathematical formulation, intuition, training dynamics, memory tradeoffs, and typical placement in transformer layers. Explain how LoRA enables finetuning with few parameters and why adapter gradients still incur activation-memory costs.
sections: LoRA: matrix factorization view and the adapter equation
Choosing the rank, scaling factor, and placement of adapters
Backpropagation with frozen base model weights: gradients flow and computational graph
Memory analysis: adapter parameters vs activation gradients vs base weights
Common PEFT alternatives and when to prefer LoRA
Empirical observations about adapter capacity and where to add adapters

outline.chapter_title: 5. Memory and Optimizer Design for Large-Scale Finetuning
outline.description: Explore the role of optimizers and optimizer states in memory use. Discuss gradient checkpointing, memory spikes from long sequences, and strategies to manage optimizer memory. Introduce the concept of paged optimizers at a high level.
sections: Popular optimizers (Adam, SGD variants) and their memory footprints
Optimizer state breakdown and scaling with model size
Gradient checkpointing mechanics and its memory/time tradeoffs
Memory spikes: causes and examples (long sequences, batching)
Techniques to reduce optimizer memory: sharding, quantized states, and paging
Introduction to Paged Optimizers and unified memory

outline.description: Give a complete conceptual walkthrough of QLoRA: the storage/computation datatypes, runtime dequantization, where LoRA fits, and how training proceeds. This chapter connects the previous background chapters into a single coherent method.
sections: Storage vs computation data types in QLoRA
End-to-end QLoRA forward and backward pass (conceptual)
Role of NF4, Double Quantization, and Paged Optimizers in the pipeline
Which tensors are quantized and which remain high precision
High-level algorithm/pseudocode and runtime considerations
Safety checks and correctness guarantees

outline.description: Present the derivation and motivation for NormalFloat (NFk) data types, focusing on NF4. Explain quantile quantization and why NF4 is information-theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights. Provide step-by-step construction and practical concerns (zero representation, asymmetric bins).
sections: Recap: quantile quantization and optimal binning for arbitrary distributions
Why weights are approximately normally distributed: empirical evidence
Deriving NormalFloat for standard normal: computing k-bit quantiles
Converting theoretical quantiles to a practical NFk datatype
Handling zero exactly: asymmetric binning and zeropoint design
Practical NF4 values and lookup tables
Empirical comparison: NF4 vs FP4 vs Int4 on standard tasks

outline.description: Explain Double Quantization: the idea of quantizing the quantization constants to save memory. Walk through the math, block size choices, benefits and tradeoffs, and how double dequantization is performed during training.

Formulating the two-level quantization process
Choice of datatypes for first and second level (NF4 for weights, FP8 for constants)

Dequantization chaining: correctness and numerical stability
Ablation studies: performance impact vs memory saved

outline.description: Provide a practical guide to using paged optimizers with modern GPU platforms. Explain unified memory, how paging works, performance implications, and when and how to deploy paged optimizers safely.

When paging happens: sources of memory pressure
Performance tradeoffs and empirical measurements
Best practices: batch sizing, sequence lengths, and when to avoid paging
Troubleshooting: common pitfalls and mitigation techniques

outline.chapter_title: 10. Backpropagating Through Quantized Weights: Math and Implementation
outline.description: Derive how gradients propagate when base model weights are stored quantized and frozen, while adapters are trainable. Explain dequantization in the forward and the role of autograd in computing gradients wrt adapters. Cover numerical precision, stability, and efficient kernel design considerations.

Computing dE/dL (adapter gradients) via dequantized intermediate tensors
Precision analysis: why BF16/BFloat is suitable for computation
Implementation patterns: eager dequantization vs on-the-fly dequant kernels
Hardware considerations for fused kernels and memory locality
Testing correctness: numerical checks and unit tests

outline.description: Present the core experimental results comparing QLoRA to 16-bit finetuning and 16-bit LoRA. Include ablations that justify NF4, double quantization, LoRA placement, and paged optimizers. Discuss interpretation and limitations of the experimental findings.
